name: K12
line: K12, an online school, teaches math one course at a time. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous.
description: AMP vs K12: online schools that teach math one course at a time, and a math program where assessment, teaching and review are continuous.
verdict: K12 runs online schools and offers single courses. Math is one course among many, taught through live classes and lessons in its schools, with a Learning Coach at home [1][3]. Its 3rd Grade Math course has a mid-year test and an end-of-year test [12]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous: every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test and no test day. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. K12 teaches math one course at a time. Its 3rd Grade Math course has a mid-year test and an end-of-year test [4][12].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem in front of the learner: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. At K12 the unit is the course, one per grade or subject [4]. In its schools, the day includes scheduled live classes with certified teachers, and the curriculum mixes interactive games, videos and hands-on activities [1][7]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [14].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, from counting through precalculus on one map of skills. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels, and repeated misses send practice back to what a skill builds on. In K12's Learning Store, math comes one course per grade or subject, from kindergarten through Calculus, and the family picks the course [4].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. K12's 3rd Grade Math course runs unit by unit, with a mid-year test and an end-of-year test [12]. We found no scheduled review of earlier skills in the pages we read [7][12]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13].

reasons.title: What the adult does
reasons.body: In AMP the adult does not plan, teach or grade. Parents and teachers see a level for each part of math and the actual problems behind every number, and each lesson has a guide for the adult. In K12's homeschool program, a Learning Coach, typically a parent or guardian, guides the student through lessons [3]. K12's Learning Store rates parent involvement in 3rd Grade Math as high, with active daily involvement, and in Algebra 1 as low [12][11].

rows.range: Schools from kindergarten through grade 12 [2]. Math courses run through Calculus [4].
rows.start: Math comes one course per grade or subject. The family picks the course [4].
rows.teaching: In its schools, live classes with certified teachers. The curriculum mixes interactive games, videos and hands-on activities [1][7].
rows.next: The course's lessons, guided by a Learning Coach [3]. K12 says its curriculum adapts to each student; the page does not say how [7].
rows.mastery: Courses run unit by unit. 3rd Grade Math has a mid-year test and an end-of-year test [12].
rows.review: No scheduled review of earlier skills found in the pages we read [7][12].
rows.print: Its schools provide books and supplies [1]. Single courses are digital; some math courses offer a materials kit [12].
rows.adult: A Learning Coach, typically a parent or guardian, guides the student through lessons [3]. In its schools, certified teachers teach [1].
rows.reports: Single courses are computer-graded [11]. The Learning Hub tracks each child's progress for the parent [6].
rows.evidence: No rating in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [8][9]. A company survey of graduates, with self-reported answers [10].

theirs: K12 is a brand of Stride, Inc. It runs online public schools and online private schools, such as K12 Private Academy and The Keystone School, from kindergarten through grade 12 [1][2]. Math is one course among many.

In its schools, the day includes scheduled live classes with certified teachers, and the curriculum mixes interactive games, videos and hands-on activities [1][7]. A parent or other responsible adult acts as the student's Learning Coach and guides the student through lessons [1][3]. K12 also offers single courses to families who teach at home, with math from kindergarten through Calculus [4]. Algebra 1 can be taken as independent study or with teacher support [11].
credit: Certified teachers and scheduled live classes in its schools [1].
Tutoring by certified teachers in math through Calculus, Statistics and Linear Algebra [5].
Math courses through Calculus, with optional teacher support [4][11].

theirs: We found no study of K12's math courses. When we checked, K12 and Stride had no rating in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [8][9].

K12's own evidence is a survey. On its Graduate Success page, K12's Future Readiness Survey found 74% of graduates of K12-powered schools optimistic about their career direction, against 56% of graduates of traditional schools [10]. The answers are self-reported, and the page gives no test scores.
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed, spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13]. A meta-analysis of 55 studies found that worked examples improve mathematics performance [14]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want a full school, with certified teachers and live classes.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want math the adult does not have to plan, teach or grade.

questions.question: How is AMP different from K12?
questions.answer: K12 runs online schools and offers single courses. Math is one course among many, with a Learning Coach guiding lessons [1][3]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does K12 work?
questions.answer: We found no study of K12's math courses. When we checked, K12 had no rating in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [8][9]. It publishes a survey of its graduates, with self-reported answers [10].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever school they attend.
